packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of these faces. packet.json was not read.

GENERAL WARNING
The script on these faces is so darkened, rubbed and (in the photographs) soft that almost no word can be read with confidence. What follows is mostly a record of letter shapes, not of words. Every reading below is tentative even where no question mark stands.

FACE A (overview image-001.jpg; tiles image-002.jpg upper, image-003.jpg lower)
Layout observations:
- A small upright strip of parchment, much taller than wide, heavily browned. Thick cord whip-stitching runs down the whole left edge, with knots at top and bottom left; the strip was evidently reused as part of a sewn object or binding.
- One narrow block of writing, about 18-19 short lines, each holding only two to four words; left margin lost under the stitching, right edge with a small blank margin. Whether this is a full column or a slice out of a wider column cannot be told from the image; the lines look cut at the left.
- A red mark (a paragraph sign or small red initial) at the left of about line 14, beside the stitching. A trace of red at the extreme top left edge. No running title, no underlining, no gloss visible.
- Hole in line 2. Lower third very dark.

image-002.jpg (upper half of Face A; 10 lines)
image-002 l.1: [dark, c. 6 letters lost] [..]mor(um)? id?/ad?
image-002 l.2: [.]i[hole][...] [.]? euā?/eiā?
image-002 l.3: [.]ss[.]a[..]u[..]u[.]aō? [a long s pair near the start; ends in a letter with a suspension stroke]
image-002 l.4: inipe[..]d[..]? s[.]li?/sibi?
image-002 l.5: [.]ene[.]i[..]a q(ue)? eos?
image-002 l.6: [.]ch[..]dij? [..]trah?/[..]rali?
image-002 l.7: [..]ipides?/[..]nd[..]s? m[..]at?
image-002 l.8: [..]u[.] [.]et[..]? [...]
image-002 l.9: [.] vnā? [..]n[....]
image-002 l.10: [...]o[.]a[..] [cropped by the foot of the tile; see image-003]

image-003.jpg (lower half of Face A; 10 lines; l.1-2 repeat image-002 l.9-10)
image-003 l.1: [.] vnā? [..]n[....]   [= image-002 l.9]
image-003 l.2: [.....]onatu[.]?/[..]orati[.]?   [= image-002 l.10]
image-003 l.3: [.]non? [..] [.]sfer?/[.]ssit?
image-003 l.4: [......] [.]t? a[..]or[.]l?
image-003 l.5: [.......] ped[.]?/p(ro)ib?
image-003 l.6: [red paragraph mark or small red initial at left] [...] [.]rali?/[.]rati?
image-003 l.7: [illegible - surface rubbed, only specks of ink]
image-003 l.8: [illegible - a few ascenders only]
image-003 l.9: [dark] [......] aqu[..]?/aqui[.]?
image-003 l.10: [dark] [....] sit? al[..]?
Below l.10 the strip ends in a ragged edge; no further line is visible.

FACE B (overview image-004.jpg; tiles image-005.jpg upper, image-006.jpg lower)
Layout observations:
- Same outline as Face A mirrored: the cord stitching is now on the right edge, so this looks like the other side of the same strip (interpretation from shape, hole position and stitching, not certain).
- Blank margin about a quarter of the width at the left; then one narrow block of about 17 lines. A straight vertical line (ruling or a crease/cut) runs down the right side of the block; a little writing and some red continue to the right of it, under the stitching. So the block may be the left part of a column, or a column followed by an intercolumn and the start of another; the crop does not decide this.
- A large red initial, two lines high, standing in the left margin at lines 6-7. Its shape is a round bowl with a tall stem at the right ending in dots above and below: read as Q, less likely a d-shaped letter.
- A red capital I inside the line at line 12. Red patches at the right edge by lines 4, 6 and 14 (under the stitching; shapes not readable). A red mark at the lower left by line 16-17 (paragraph mark or initial).
- Hole in line 2 (matches the hole of Face A). No running title, underlining or gloss seen.

image-005 l.2: [.]me? d(e)? l[hole][..]mi[.]? [.]
image-005 l.3: o[.]erāt?/aderūt? nia?/via? [..] de?
image-005 l.4: g[..]? h(uius)?/hy[.] sta[..]? [red patch at right]

image-005 l.10: [.]a[.]i[.]? n[..] [...]

image-006 l.2: [.]a[.]i[.]? n[..] [...]   [= image-005 l.10]
image-006 l.3: seo?/sco(rum)? h[.]? [.]oq(ue)? [..]dy[.]?
image-006 l.4: nōm[.]n?/aīmar(um)? [red capital I] n[..]
image-006 l.5: me?/ine? . Ip(s)e?/Jp[..]? [..]i? [..]
image-006 l.6: si[....]ar(um)? ei(us)? [..]d?/[..]b?
image-006 l.7: t[.]? e in?/em? d[.]o?/[.]b[.]? sua(m)?/suoru[.]? [red patch at right]
image-006 l.8: [....]nd[..]? [..]ai[..]?
image-006 l.9: [..]d[..]o[..]? hu[..]?/ha[..]?
image-006 l.10: [red mark at far left] d[.]i[...] [...]
image-006 l.11: [dark traces only at the ragged foot]

FACE C (overview image-007.jpg; tiles image-008.jpg upper, image-009.jpg lower)
Layout observations:
- A second strip of the same general size, or the same object from another side: here the right edge carries separate cord stitches (not the continuous whip-stitch of Faces A/B), which makes me think this is a different strip. That is an inference from the stitching only.
- Blank margin at the left; one narrow block of about 18 short lines; text runs under the stitches at the right.
- A red initial in the left margin at about line 16, shaped like a D or round O with a spur at upper left (read as D?). A small red stroke at the left of about line 14. A red patch at the right of line 2 under the stitches, and a red sign like a letter with a bar over it (ā?) at the right of line 13.
- Very dark brown staining over the middle and left; lines 6-12 are almost lost. No running title, underlining or gloss seen.

image-008.jpg (upper part of Face C; 11 lines)
image-008 l.1: D[.]o[.]i[.]us?/Dyon[...]? d[.] p[..]?   [first word begins the line; shape suggests a long word of minims]
image-008 l.2: [.]Remig[..]?/[.]kemp[..]? [red patch under stitches]
image-008 l.3: [.]o[.]d[.]s?/fid[..]? p[..]
image-008 l.4: [.] face[.]?/sacer? [.]n[..]
image-008 l.5: a?greg[.]?/[.]tgreg[..]? [.]a[..]
image-008 l.6: [...] g[..]m[..]?
image-008 l.7: g[..] [.] A[..]? [a horizontal stroke through the line]
image-008 l.8: [illegible - stained]
image-008 l.9: [..]usta[..]?/[..]ussin[.]?
image-008 l.10: [..]ile[..]?
image-008 l.11: [..]uc[..] [.]de? a[..]   [cropped at the foot of the tile]
Note: l.1, l.2 and l.5 each look as if they open with a word that could be a personal name; I record that as an impression of word shape only and do not read the names with confidence.

image-009.jpg (lower part of Face C; 10 lines; l.1-2 repeat image-008 l.10-11)
image-009 l.1: [..]ile[..]?   [= image-008 l.10]
image-009 l.2: [..]uc[..] [.]de? a[..]   [= image-008 l.11]
image-009 l.3: [..]c? op[.]u[.]d[.]?/[..]pt[.]ind[.]?
image-009 l.4: [.]dar[.]?/[.]dor[.]? [.]e[..]
image-009 l.5: b[..]d[..]? [..] [red sign at right: a with a bar above?]
image-009 l.6: [small red stroke at left] [illegible]
image-009 l.7: [..]uc[.]a[..]?/[..]nit[.]a[..]? [...]
image-009 l.8: [red initial D? in the left margin] [text of the line illegible]
image-009 l.9: [illegible]
image-009 l.10: [..]mi[...]? [last line at the ragged foot]

FACE D (overview image-010.jpg; tiles image-011.jpg upper, image-012.jpg lower)
Layout observations:
- Mirror outline of Face C (stitching now on the left, knotted cords), so probably the other side of that strip; inference from shape only.
- A straight vertical line (ruling, crease or cut) runs down the strip about a third of the way in from the left. Writing stands on both sides of it; to the left of it only two to five letters per line survive beside the stitching. This may be the end of one column and the start of the next, or one column crossed by a crease; I cannot decide from the image.
- Red heading in the top line, to the right of the vertical line: a short word with long s and a superscript abbreviation sign, followed by a numeral that reads iiij.
- A red initial L (or a red paragraph sign of that shape) at the far left by line 4, under the stitching; red marks at the far left by line 10; a small red tick on the vertical line at about line 15 and another at the foot. A green stain or spot in line 15 and green tinges at the left of lines 3-5 and 11 (stain, not pigment decoration as far as I can tell).
- No running title other than the red heading, no underlining, no gloss seen. This is the least darkened of the four faces, but the ink is thin and blurred.

image-011.jpg (upper part of Face D; 11 lines)
image-011 l.1: [left of the line: dark traces] | [red] [.]p[.]is[..]?/Ep(isto)la?/[.]pisc[.]? iiij
image-011 l.2: o ve[..]? | [.]aurēd?/[.]aucēd? aq̄?/ad?
image-011 l.3: [...] | [.]e? sus[..]me?/suscipe?
image-011 l.4: [red L at far left] [....] | [.]a? a sanct[.]?/a simil[.]?
image-011 l.5: [....] | illum? ecia(m)?/et sine?
image-011 l.6: [....] | [.]os? a[.]t? in d(omi)ni?/ī mō[.]i?
image-011 l.7: [.] le[..]? | [.]ī[.]s? [..]mur?/[..]uit?
image-011 l.8: [....] | [.]sp[..]q[.]? [..]a[..]
image-011 l.9: [...] | [.]illius? e[.]se?/ecia(m)?
image-011 l.10: [red marks at far left] [....] | [..]sta?/[..]sca? mes?/ines?
image-011 l.11: [...] | [..]n[.]? uue[.]g?   [cropped at the foot of the tile]

image-012.jpg (lower part of Face D; 11 lines; l.1-3 repeat image-011 l.9-11)
image-012 l.1: [...] | [.]illius? e[.]se?   [= image-011 l.9]
image-012 l.2: [red marks at far left] | [..]sta? mes?   [= image-011 l.10]
image-012 l.3: [.]t?[..] | [..]ne? uue[.]g?/uiueq(ue)?   [= image-011 l.11]
image-012 l.4: b[...] | [..]a[.]i? ih[.]?/ib[.]?
image-012 l.5: [...] | [.]ius[.]i? ilig[..]?/diligit?
image-012 l.6: [.]e[.]e[..] | [..]is? [.]si?/[.]ssi?
image-012 l.7: [...] [red tick on the vertical line] | [green spot] [..]mi[..]
image-012 l.8: [...] | [illegible]
image-012 l.9: [...] | [..]i[.]o[..]?
image-012 l.10: [...] | [..]a[.]o[.]? lib[..]?/hb[..]?
image-012 l.11: [...] [red tick] | [..]d[.]j? simile?/[..]mulo? [..]

LIMITATIONS AND NOTES (PACKET-02)
- Four faces, apparently two small strips photographed on both sides, both reused with cord stitching along one long edge. Each face holds one narrow block of roughly 17-19 very short lines.
- I could not produce connected text on any face. No span of ten readable lines exists in these images at this quality. The entries above are letter-shape records with heavy uncertainty; none should be used as a secure reading for a source match. The most nearly secure items are: the red heading with numeral iiij on Face D (image-011 l.1); the large red initial (Q?) on Face B and the red capital I in image-006 l.4; the red initial (D?) on Face C; "sus..." on Face D l.3; and the word shapes at the head of Face C lines 1, 2 and 5.
- Line beginnings on Faces A and D and line ends on Faces B and C lie under the stitching and are lost in these images.
- The tiles are sharp on the cord fibres but the script itself is blurred (ink spread, staining). A higher-resolution or raking-light capture would not obviously help; an infrared or UV capture is what I would ask for, especially for Faces A and C. A wider view showing how the two strips sit in their host object would help with column order and with whether Faces A/B and C/D come from the same leaf.
- Beyond the rules: on image-002.jpg I made two contrast-stretched grayscale crops into a scratch folder (work/crops-reader/) to try to recover letters; they did not improve the reading and I did not repeat this for the other tiles. No other file, directory, web source or search tool was used, and packet.json was not read.
